_doc: VALLEY REGION (chapters 1-2) — refinement of world.json's 'valley' envelope.
STORY GEOGRAPHY (user, 2026-07-30; RESTAMPED to the user's ruling of 2026-08-01):
the Whisperwood highland bowl (SW) is sealed from the valley by the gatewall spur;
Emberbrook sits against the wall with ONE forest entrance, arriving from the SOUTH.
THE RIVER IS BORN DEEP IN THE WHISPERWOOD, upstream of the village: it runs NORTH
past Emberbrook's east side, under the Old Gate through the notch it cut, over Ember
Falls at the gatewall's foot, and then NORTH-EAST down the gorge to Dellhollow and on
toward an eventual estuary and the sea (schematic, late-game). The river runs in a
STEEP CANYON: the road descends a bench on the WEST wall — the LEFT bank looking
downstream, the village's own bank, the Old Gate's bank and Dellhollow's — and the far
(EAST) wall is tall unclimbable cliff topped by visible-but-unreachable forest (ch3
territory). No crossings CAN exist; onward is downriver through Dellhollow. Deep forest
is represented as CANOPY MASS (continuous undulating treetop surface, WALKABLE-UNDER,
veg_-prefixed), not standalone tree copies — specimen trees only at edges, clearings,
and the road corridor. ONE canonical scene: ow-valley, updated in place (no new keys).

GATING PRINCIPLE (user, 2026-07-30): forests are always walkable encounter terrain (FF9 model) — Whisperwood is gated by STRONG ENEMIES, not geometry. Hard restriction comes ONLY from height-based geography (unclimbable walls, undescendable cliffs).

THE TOWN->REGION IMPRESSION TRANSFORM (derived 2026-08-01, coordinator-stamped at checkpoint 1). Every town-adjacent seat in this file is derived, not authored: world = anchor.pos + scale * R(rotationDeg) * M * (townPos - origin), M = diag(1,-1) when townAnchors[].impression.mirrorY. origin is the centroid of the town map's SETTLED landmarks; scale is impressionRadius / the p90 radius of that set, so the impression disc IS the settled town. Emberbrook 0.3232 u/m (1u = 3.09 m), confirmed independently by the arrival leg at 0.3074 (within 5%). Dellhollow 0.4348 u/m AND MIRRORED: its map frame is LEFT-HANDED against the world (+x downstream = NE = rotationDeg 33; +y cliff->river = world ESE = downstream MINUS 90), so a plain rotation reflects the town. That trap is stated here because it is invisible in the numbers and fatal in the build.

THE PINCH-RATIO RULE (ratified 2026-08-01 as standing doctrine, not one seat's fix): A PINCH IS SEATED BY RATIO, NOT METRES. The world's river is not the town's river shrunk — at the Old Gate the town's 6.95 m grate scales to 2.25u against a ratified parent width of 4.60u, a factor of 2 — so carrying the town's METRES across puts the gate doorway's east jamb in the water, which is the failure the previous re-seat shipped and only a rendered frame caught. Carry the RATIOS instead: the doorway centre stands 2.727 channel half-widths off the centreline and the founded wall keeps 1.022 half-widths of dry ground. Both are scale-free statements the two maps can make about the same pinch. Evidence the frame is right and not fitted: the town's own downstream-vista falls out at 4.08u east of the channel against a 2.30u half-width — on the FAR bank looking back through the gap, exactly as its map note claims.

elevation._doc: highland bowl h~26 SW of the gatewall, and the river is born INSIDE it; the WEST left-bank side is HIGH LAND (road 26.5->12, land 26->9) with the river cutting an ever-deeper canyon below it downstream of Ember Falls; the far EAST wall rises to a comparable forested plateau.

plateau.note: the Whisperwood highland — unioned with the Emberbrook anchor disc; the river's springs rise in its southern reach

canyon._doc: asymmetric trench along the whole spine. benchSide W = HIGH LAND: the road holds plateau height (clearance grows downstream as the river cuts deeper), comparable to the far EAST wall top; Dellhollow is the slope descending off the high land into the gorge. farPlateau tops the unreachable EAST side. Upstream of the Old Gate the trench is barely a trench at all — a gentle valley floor with the river a metre or two below its banks, which is what the Emberbrook town map builds.

waterAccess.note: the Moorage: the ONLY bench-side descent to water. It is a BREACH — the bench profile, the shelf wall AND the rim all yield here, which they did not before: the north rim went on standing where the landing had to be.

shelf._doc: the valley path is a NARROW LEDGE hard against a HIGH mountain wall on the player's LEFT (away from the river, which is on the right the whole way down): restricted first-act overworld, open world saved for later

pockets.note: a broad natural terrace mid-descent on the road's own bank, filled with walkable forest

overrun._doc: the ridge continues past Dellhollow along the gorge rim and pinches out naturally — the ledge is terrain, not an A-to-B corridor

canyon._doc_benchSide: CHIRALITY, RESTAMPED 2026-08-01: with downstream now NORTH-EAST the traversable bench is the WEST bank, which is the LEFT bank looking downstream — the mirror of the value this file used to carry (the south-west side, right bank). tools/valley_map.py currently hardcodes the bench to the RIGHT bank (sideL == 0) and MUST be made to read this field before ow-valley is rebuilt, or the canyon will be carved the wrong way round.

river._doc: Refined course of the spine, source to handoff: born in the Whisperwood springs, north past Emberbrook's east bank, under the Old Gate, over Ember Falls, north-east down the gorge. Parent width profile 2->28.

road._doc: Whisperwood entrance (from the SOUTH, beside the water on the river's west bank) -> Emberbrook -> the Old Gate at the village's north shoulder (the road's doorway beside the water grate, both on the village's own WEST bank) -> down the gorge's WEST (left-bank) wall -> Dellhollow's Valley Gate. NEVER CROSSES, and never needs to: the river is on the traveller's right from the first step to the last. The old reading, in which the road met no water at all above the gate, is DEAD: the river is beside the road from the arrival clearing onward, and it is why Vesper's road exists.

portals.note: map-edge fiction entrance, south up the river's west bank; not traversable in ch1-2

town entry — the ONE way in from the forest. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-01 from emberbrook.map.json's own 'road-gate' (the timber arch over the south road, harvest wreaths), 42.1 m from the settled centroid = 13.62u at the impression scale: the impression's rim, not its middle.
the cut through the gatewall, on the village's west bank; the only forest->valley passage. Vesper's bottleneck.
the town model's clifftop Valley Gate; WEST rim, left bank, the road's side

corridor.note: the road cuts a corridor through the canopy; Emberbrook sits in a cleared pocket

forests.note: DEEP forest: continuous canopy mass, WALKABLE beneath (encounter terrain — strong-enemy gated, not geometry-gated); specimen trees at edges/corridor; the road corridor is the safe path
atop the far (EAST) canyon wall - unreachable because the CLIFF is unclimbable (height gating), the forest itself is ordinary walkable canopy
open left-bank woodland above the road: standalone trees, walkable between
walkable-under canopy forest filling the pocket terrace; the road keeps its corridor through it

crossings._doc: NONE — and none possible: the canyon geometry enforces it. Dellhollow's dam crest is the only span of the river in the world so far.
crossings.note: AND THE ROAD NEVER NEEDS ONE: the Emberbrook->Dellhollow road descends the gorge on the WEST wall — the village's bank, the Old Gate's bank — with the river on the traveller's right the whole way. Where the road DOES cross is Dellhollow's dam crest (the dam-crest-gate landmark in townmap/dellhollow.map.json), which makes the world's only span the FIRST CROSSING OF THE GAME — and it is barred shut this chapter, no far-side town yet. No village bridge, and no other bridge anywhere (coordinator's ruling, 2026-08-01, on the user's delegation).

landmarks.note: the Whisperwood waystone where the corridor breaks out onto the bench below the Old Gate; snapped ON the road ribbon (valley_verify probes its zone cell)
the tar-dark boat at the Moorage water access

townAnchors.note: warm-lit clearing town against the gatewall, the river along its east side flowing NORTH and the Old Gate visible at its north shoulder; rotationDeg 0 — the town map's north IS world north, which is what makes the arrival read south and the gate north

impression._doc: THE TOWN->REGION IMPRESSION TRANSFORM, written down for the first time: world = pos + scale * R(rotationDeg) * M * (townPos - origin), M = diag(1,-1) when mirrorY. origin is the centroid of the town map's SETTLED landmarks (its out-of-town road and gate group excluded); scale is impressionRadius / the p90 radius of that set, so the impression disc IS the settled town. Emberbrook: 35 landmarks, p90 43.31 m, 14u/43.31 m = 0.3232 u/m (1u = 3.09 m). Checked independently against the arrival leg (78.3 m of town road vs the ratified 24.08u) = 0.3074, within 5%.

townAnchors.note: canyon-straddling impression, mass on the WEST (left) bank per the road's own side; stepped clusters, weir flight, wheels; entry notch on the WEST rim. rotationDeg 33 = the downstream heading here, so the town map's local +x (along-gorge, downstream) points north-east. NOTE FOR THE TOWN LANE: dellhollow.map.json's local +y runs from the town's near wall out to the river, and in this frame that is the world's EAST/SE side — so its units line's compass labels ('north positive', 'near (south) wall') are LOCAL labels, superseded by this anchor. Not edited here (town maps are not this lane's); flagged for a restate.

impression._doc: GATE-ANCHORED (coordinator ruling 2026-08-01, on the user's delegation). THE PIN IS THE VALLEY GATE, not the centroid, because the gate is the only LOAD-BEARING dot this town has on the tile — it is the portal, the region spawn and the road's end — while the Moorage and the locks are scenery. THE SCALE IS THE ONE THAT SEAT IMPLIES: 8.94u of world per 33.61 m of town = 0.2661 u/m. Chosen over the Moorage-implied 0.5171 because gate-scale keeps Dellhollow's miniature COMPARABLE TO EMBERBROOK's derived 0.3232 (ratio 0.82), so relative town sizes read honestly on the world map; the Moorage scale would have drawn Dellhollow 60% larger per metre than Emberbrook for no reason but which dot was picked. impressionRadius follows the scale, 18 -> 11.0: a COMPACT town. IF DELLHOLLOW SHOULD READ MORE SUBSTANTIAL ON THE TILE, THE APPROVED LEVER IS MORE DRAWN ROOFTOPS DOWN THE GORGE in the impression, not a bigger radius — the radius is now a derived quantity and changing it re-lies about the town's size. ACROSS the gorge the town's y (cliff 0 -> river ~30) is carried as a RATIO of the channel's own half-width, not as metres: the pinch-ratio rule, for the same reason it exists at the Old Gate — the world channel is far wider than this map's frame allows for, and metres put the quay, the locks and the Moorage under water.

zoneOverrides.note: the far (EAST) canyon wall is crag regardless of slope thresholds
